title: Novel App knock-in mouse model shows key features of amyloid pathology and reveals profound metabolic dysregulation of microglia

evidence_spans.quote: Methods We engineered a novel App knock-in mouse model
Amyloid-β pathology, neurodegeneration, glial responses, brain metabolism and behavioral phenotypes were characterized
a hyperactivity phenotype as the animals aged

scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This primary mouse study analyzes Alzheimer’s disease pathology. Age is used to describe disease-model progression, without an explicit analysis or interpretation of an aging construct; therefore multi-omics is not assessed.

causal_design_reviewer.exposure_or_intervention: App SAA knock-in genotype carrying Swedish, Arctic, and Austrian App mutations
causal_design_reviewer.comparator: Wild type littermate mice (and heterozygous versus homozygous App SAA mice)
causal_design_reviewer.outcome: Amyloid pathology, neurodegeneration, glial responses, brain metabolism, behavioral phenotypes, and microglial lipid/metabolite and transcriptomic alterations
causal_design_reviewer.estimand_or_contrast: Outcomes characterized across heterozygous and homozygous App SAA mice with wild type littermates as experimental controls

evidence_spans.quote: We engineered a novel App knock-in mouse model ... using homologous recombination to introduce three disease-causing coding mutations
heterozygous and homozygous App SAA mice

Wild type littermate mice were used as experimental controls

causal_design_reviewer.concise_rationale: The current report applies a direct genetic knock-in perturbation and compares characterized outcomes with wild-type experimental controls.
